Folks — technical attestation and clarifications below (for the single-sheet and checklist):

Summary (short):
- Data plane segmentation: Customers may choose EU, US or APAC region at onboarding. All persisted tokens, embeddings, logs that are required for model inference are stored in the selected region.
- KMS/Keying: We support customer-managed KMS (bring-your-own-key) in EU and US regions. Keys are configured in the customer's cloud tenant or via a customer KMS instance integrated with our private deployment. Key metadata for routing is stored in the control plane only.
- Telemetry and metrics: Default telemetry is aggregated at control plane level (hosted) for service health. For Private/Dedicated customers, telemetry aggregation can be configured to remain in-region.
- Failover behavior:
  * Active region failover is an opt-in feature. If enabled, data replication for failover is explicitly configured in the onboarding runbook and must be accepted by the customer’s admin.
  * We will not automatically replicate EU-stored customer data to US/APAC without activation steps or a contractual exception.
- Backup & snapshots: periodic backups are stored encrypted. By default backups remain in-region; cross-region snapshot copy is configurable and documented in the runbook.
- Audit logs: Per-request audit trails with timestamps and site-of-processing markers are available for export from the EU logging endpoint (EU-only) and can be included in the evidence package.

Suggested single-sheet bullets (to copy into the customer doc):
- "Redwood stores inference data (model inputs/outputs and embeddings) in the customer-selected region by default.
- Cross-region transfer only occurs with customer opt-in, contractual approval, or legal compulsion.
- Customer-managed KMS supported in EU/US for key jurisdiction control.
- Per-request audit logs can be delivered from regional logging endpoints for compliance review"

I'll attach a short example audit-export command and the runbook snippet for activation gates.

Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Architect — Redwood Inference
